description: Business questions with known-correct answers. The expected values are derived from ground truth, not from a previous run of the agent, so these can fail.

cases.question: which variant had the highest revenue lift in checkout_flow_v2 over the last 56 days
cases.notes: Truth: treatment_b revenue lift +25.35%. Guardrail trap: treatment_c passes conversion but fails revenue.

cases.question: which variant had the highest revenue lift in checkout_flow_v2 over the last 30 days
cases.notes: Shorter window, same winner. Tests that the date parser is not just grabbing everything.

cases.question: which variant had the highest purchase rate lift in pricing_page_copy_v3 over the last 42 days
cases.notes: True effect is exactly zero. A readout that claims a winner here is wrong.

cases.question: which variant had the highest purchase rate lift in onboarding_email_v1 over the last 35 days
cases.notes: Real +14% effect, but assignment was 60/40. SRM must be surfaced in the answer text.

cases.question: was there a sample ratio mismatch in onboarding_email_v1
cases.notes: Direct SRM question. Truth: 60/40 observed vs 50/50 intended.

cases.question: is the variant split balanced in checkout_flow_v2
cases.notes: checkout_flow_v2 has no SRM. Must not cry wolf.

cases.question: show me the daily revenue trend per variant for checkout_flow_v2 over the last 56 days
cases.notes: Trend shape. Revenue per user is flat-ish over a test window; the point is 56 days x 3 variants.

cases.question: purchase rate by country in checkout_flow_v2 over the last 56 days
cases.notes: 7 countries in the data. Segment breakdown must come from a query, not a guess.

cases.question: revenue per user by device for pricing_page_copy_v3 over the last 42 days
cases.notes: 'device' must resolve to the platform column.

cases.question: which variant had the highest sessions per user lift in onboarding_email_v1 over the last 35 days
cases.notes: Truth is +9% sessions, a real effect, but this experiment has a 60/40 SRM. Correct behaviour is to surface the effect and refuse to name a winner.

cases.question: what is the average order value lift for treatment_c in checkout_flow_v2 over the last 56 days
cases.notes: treatment_c AOV truth is -14%, so this must report a REGRESSION, not name a winner. AOV is measured over purchasers only.

cases.question: how long do we need to run checkout_flow_v2 to detect a 5% lift
cases.notes: Sample-size math from the catalog. No query needed; the answer is a formula.

cases.question: how long do we need to run checkout_flow_v2 to detect a 10% lift
cases.notes: A 10% MDE needs a bigger sample than a 5% MDE. Monotonicity check.
